t: You're at the Royal Naval Division Memorial on Horse Guards Parade, a First World War memorial to members of the 63rd Division who were killed. It was unveiled on the twenty-fifth of April 1925, ten years to the day after the Gallipoli landings, where the division suffered heavy casualties. Former members of the division raised the funds, through a committee chaired by Brigadier-General Arthur Asquith. When the navy dropped a larger Trafalgar Square monument, they went ahead alone and engaged Sir Edwin Lutyens. Eric Broadbent and Frederick Wilcoxson were the sculptors.
